output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: multiple parsers/factories (PropertiesParser, XmlParser, PropertyFactory, MappingUtil, ConsoleOperations) reflectively instantiated a class named by attacker-controlled input (property `type` attribute, flip-strategy `class` attribute/JSON field, or the web console's `strategy` HTTP parameter) and only checked the resulting object's type via a cast *after* construction. This let an attacker force instantiation (constructor execution, incl. static initializers) of an arbitrary class on the classpath — classic CWE-094 "improper control of generation of code" via unrestricted reflection.

Fix: introduced `MappingUtil.loadClass(String className, Class<T> expectedType)`, which resolves the class and validates `expectedType.isAssignableFrom(clazz)` before returning it — no instantiation happens for a class that isn't actually a `Property` or `FlippingStrategy` subtype. Replaced every direct `Class.forName(...).newInstance()`/`getConstructor(...).newInstance()` sink that took an externally-supplied class name with this checked helper:
  - `MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy` (used by nearly every store mapper/JSON parser/AOP advisor across the codebase)
  - `PropertyFactory.createProperty(String,String,String,String,Set)` (used by nearly every store mapper/JSON parser/controller)
  - `XmlParser.parsePropertiesTag` and `XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy` (duplicated the same pattern outside the shared helpers)
  - `PropertiesParser.parseProperties` and `PropertiesParser.parseFeatures` (same duplication for the `.properties`-based config parser)
  - `ConsoleOperations.createFeature` (the embedded web console's create-feature action, driven directly by an HTTP request parameter)

Added regression tests (`NotAPropertyClass`, `NotAFlippingStrategyClass`) that assert a same-signature-but-wrong-type class is rejected and its constructor never runs, directly proving the fix blocks construction rather than merely failing a later cast.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change is intentionally restrictive: any caller previously relying on passing a class name that does NOT implement Property/FlippingStrategy (which would previously throw only after successful construction, or previously succeed if by luck the cast never happened) will now fail fast with IllegalArgumentException/FeatureAccessException before construction — this is the intended security fix and matches the pre-existing exception types already used at these call sites, so no new checked-exception surface is introduced. All legitimate built-in Property* and FlippingStrategy implementations remain assignable and unaffected, confirmed by the full existing test suite (1129 tests) plus 2 new regression tests, all passing. No dependency or API signature changes; `MappingUtil.loadClass` is a new public static method, purely additive.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-094 reflective code-injection risk: several sinks (MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, PropertyFactory.createProperty, XmlParser's property/strategy parsing, PropertiesParser's property/strategy parsing, and the web console's ConsoleOperations.createFeature) took attacker-controlled class names (from properties/XML/JSON configs or HTTP parameters) and reflectively instantiated them via Class.forName(...).newInstance()/getConstructor(...).newInstance() BEFORE checking the resulting object was actually a Property or FlippingStrategy. This meant an attacker-chosen class's constructor (and any static initializers/side effects it triggers) would run even when the class had nothing to do with the expected type — the type mismatch only surfaced afterward as a ClassCastException. Added a new `MappingUtil.loadClass(String className, Class<T> expectedType)` helper that resolves the class and calls `expectedType.isAssignableFrom(clazz)` *before* any constructor is invoked, throwing IllegalArgumentException/FeatureAccessException instead of instantiating. Updated all five direct reflective-construction sinks (2 in MappingUtil-based callers already covered by fixing MappingUtil/PropertyFactory centrally, plus the 3 call sites in XmlParser, PropertiesParser and ConsoleOperations that duplicated the same unguarded pattern) to route through this check. Added regression tests using dummy classes with an INSTANTIATED side-effect flag to prove the constructor never runs when the class doesn't implement the expected base type.
